R306 — XeStrata b9 single-device Arc B570 safety review
Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo)
Scope: source-only comparison for one Intel Arc B570 running Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S. No build, test, device query, model/server run, GPU work, Git mutation, or artifact cleanup. This is eligibility analysis, not a performance or correctness result.

Pinned sources
- New pristine: b9f00e9db7fd56decdd9930ee84049d980b904e4
- Old pristine: da3d426079019daa6e01388d03b0d94ae67070b7
- Diff: 148 files, +15057/-1769. The new revision includes upstream Strata 0.1.43, multi-GPU integration, and newer native MoE/prefill code.
- Worktrees: /home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/MistVVK/XeStrata/.worktree/bench-xestrata-xe0142-pristine-20261012 and .../bench-xestrata-b9f00e9-pristine-20261013.

Decision
Do not approve a normal Qwen3.8 IQ3_S prefill/decode on this single B570 as a safe validation or performance run from source review alone. The model is qwen4exp and remains on the legacy generate.cpp/session.cpp doorbell path. Its CPU expert pool and GPU graph concurrently exchange mapped host-USM seq/flag words through plain volatile loads/stores. System-scope fences and volatile do not create atomic synchronization. Existing Xe source comments explicitly say no GPU reports usm_atomic_host_allocations (src/kernels/xe/elementwise.cpp:121-128), and an earlier B70 empirical probe is not evidence for Arc B570 or a portable contract. The repository's visibility probe is insufficient to qualify the data race. Until B570 is explicitly qualified or the model path is changed to a serialized handoff, any successful output would be empirical only, not a portable correctness/safety pass.

Why this is the actual model path
- include/strata/artifact/model_spec.hpp:10-14,31,133-141 labels Qwen3.8-Flash-Next as qwen4exp.
- include/strata/program/plain_generate.hpp:8-10 and src/program/generate.cpp:1989-1991 route other supported model shapes to PlainModel, but qwen4exp falls through to the Qwen3.8 engine.
- src/core/session.cpp:660-707 shows each layer graph launch followed by host polling of h_seq and CPU pool consumption of doorbell payload. It calls event_query in every poll; source comments at 672-680 say driver entry is needed for mapped-write visibility on that driver.
- src/kernels/xe/elementwise.cpp:130-163 implements volatile host reads and writes with fences; 217-233 publishes payload before incrementing seq. No atomic object synchronizes host and device.
- src/core/verify.cpp:495-500 selects segmented verification when doorbell_visible() fails, but that probe only asks whether a running kernel sees a host write. In the model's verify path, src/core/verify.cpp:1100-1102 still records doorbell_publish for the host pool. Segmented verification is not a general serialized fallback for session/token execution.

Prefill/MMQ and numerical limits
- New src/prefill/moe_mmq.cpp:21-30 dispatches int8 MMQ and quantization; lines 35-41 derive duplicated activation columns for Q2_K and pass expert row bounds/table offsets.
- New src/kernels/xe/iq_mmq.cpp:462-479 defines 16x16x16 matrix microtiles, K=128 steps, 32-lane subgroup and a local-memory layout; 493-559 bounds expert rows and masks tail rows/K. Lines 812-852 choose 16/32/64-row tiles, use 32 rows when the average rows per expert is <=32, and select guarded K-tail kernels for K not divisible by 128.
- shape_reported checks subgroup size 32 and int8/int32 matrix combinations (iq_mmq.cpp:869-880); runtime eligibility also checks local memory and a layout probe (915 onward). This is a useful dispatch gate but does not establish Arc B570 support, numerical parity, or safety of host-USM polling. It must be measured on the exact card and compiler.
- Qwen3.8’s engine uses its own prefill pipeline in src/prefill/prefill.cpp; the newly added PlainModel paths do not replace Qwen3.8. The MMQ source changes are relevant to prompt processing, not a remedy for the host/device doorbell during decode.
- docs/BUILD.md:24-30,44-66 distinguishes free DPC++ and contrib-LLVM builds; the default is contrib-LLVM, while free is Intel-only and contrib-icpx is deprecated/experimental. Exact build/runtime identity matters. No compile or runtime result was collected here.

Changes and non-changes material to this decision
- New verify code adds segmented windows when visibility probing fails; it does not change session.cpp’s host/device seq/flag protocol.
- New MMQ dispatch/tile and K-tail code expands kernels, but no evidence here establishes those kernels compile or run on this B570.
- No Qwen3.8 handoff redesign or capability gate for host/device atomic access was found in the reviewed paths. Do not infer safety from doorbell_visible(), subgroup support, matrix-shape reports, or B70 comments.

Safe next steps for Main
1. Before any model run, obtain the exact B570 device/runtime/driver/compiler identity and query host-USM plus host/device atomic capability and relevant system-scope fence support; preserve the result and command as compact evidence. If atomic-host support remains absent, do not use the live doorbell path for a correctness/performance claim.
2. Prefer a code-level serialized CPU/GPU handoff for qwen4exp, or an explicitly supported atomic protocol with matching host/device atomic object. Add a capability-based refusal/fallback; the visibility probe alone is not that check.
3. After that contract is addressed, run CPU-only MMQ unpack/quantization parity and bounds tests, then a bounded B570 kernel-only correctness/parity probe for IQ3_S and K-tail/row-tail cases. Separate correctness from timing.
4. Only then consider one-device Qwen3.8 IQ3_S prefill and decode with exact model hash, context/chunk sizes, free/contrib LLVM identity, individual samples, fault checks, and output fingerprints. Do not use multigpu, speculative, server, or RESTORE paths to stand in for this single-device question.

Limitations
This review establishes source routing and hazards only. It does not establish the B570’s actual runtime capabilities, compilation success, MMQ dispatch choice, kernel parity, fault status, or throughput. The 148-file diff also contains unrelated model, setup, multi-GPU and serving work; this report only follows paths named above.
